title: The Fan Everyone Hated for 13 Years #shorts

lines.text: The ball flew towards him, and he instinctively stuck out his hands right as the left fielder jumped for it, but his catch blocked the player's glove.
The left fielder screamed at him. The Cubs were five outs from the World Series, and this was Steve Bartman.
The umpire ruled no interference, but it was too late. The Cubs fell apart, and Florida scored eight runs that inning.
Fans threw trash at him. Security had to sneak him out of the stadium.
He apologized publicly, but he became one of baseball's most hated fans.
Thirteen years later, the Cubs finally won the World Series, and gave him a championship ring.
All for reaching at a foul ball, like fans do every game. So when a ball flies at you, do you reach?

sources: https://sabr.org/gamesproj/game/october-14-2003-the-bartman-game (Oct 14 2003, NLCS Game 6, Wrigley; Cubs 3-0, eighth inning, one out; left fielder Moises Alou; umpire Mike Everitt ruled no interference; Marlins scored 8 runs in the inning, won 8-3; Game 7 lost 9-6; security disguised and escorted him out; debris thrown; next-day apology 'so truly sorry')
https://www.npr.org/sections/thetwo-way/2017/07/31/540640239/fan-blamed-for-chicago-cubs-loss-gets-his-own-world-series-ring (Cubs won 2016 WS, 13 years after 2003; ring given July 2017)

facts.five_outs: Cubs led 3-0 with one out in the 8th: two more outs in the 8th plus three in the 9th = five outs
facts.ring: Cubs won the 2016 World Series (13 years after 2003); ring presented in 2017
facts.removed: death-threat claim not stated in the cited sources, so it is left out
